lines.li: [them] Word at home is that our peoples swore a pact.
[us] We did, and I'm glad of it.
[them,their:tribal] The elders say a blood oath binds both ways.
[them,their:medieval] The reeve read the treaty out in the market, seal and all.
[them,their:industrial] Somebody framed the signed copy and hung it in the hall.
[them,their:spacer] It's registered at home, with both sides' marks on it.
[them] Then we'll see how well it holds.
[us] If raiders come at your town, we'll come.
[them] And if they come at yours, call and we'll answer.
[us] That's what the pact is for.
[them] Our watchers look your way every night now.
[us] For a fire by our gate?
[them] For that, and we'd ride as soon as we saw it.
[them] Our caravan will be by again before the season turns.
[us] We'll have the cart ready for your porters.
[them,their:industrial] Fair prices both ways, that's the contract.
[them] Good, my people count on it now.
[them] The pact makes my work easy, I know there's a sale here every season.
[us] And we know you'll come.
[them] It was your colony that asked for the pact, I hear.
[us] It was, we'd rather have friends than walls alone.
[them] My people liked being asked.
[us] Your people offered us the pact, and we took it gladly.
[them,their:tribal] The chief doesn't offer gifts to just anyone.
[them] My people don't offer that lightly.
[them] Everyone at home is talking about the call between our peoples.
[us] Then let's hope it ends well for both of us.
[them] I put my own name to the pact, so don't make me regret it.
[us] You won't.
[them] A pact is a pact, but my people expect more of your colony.
[us] We'll keep our side of it.
[us] The pact with {PACTWITH} is the best thing we've signed in years.
[them,their:lowtech] My people will be glad to hear you say it.
[them] Then let's keep it another year when this one's done.
[us] I'd like that.
[us] The truce with {TRUCEWITH} has held so far.
[them,their:tribal] Green branches were carried, and nobody has broken them.
[them] So far, and I mean to keep it that way while I'm here.
[them] The truce runs out soon, you know.
[us] I'd rather it ended as a peace.
[them] So would I, but that's not up to me.
[us] Your people asked for this truce after that raid.
[them] We lost enough people that day, I'll say that much.
